summary: Recursive-backtracker maze generation, producing a perfect maze.
overview: Produces a "perfect" maze: exactly one path between any two cells, no loops and no isolated areas. A reference implementation on purpose, with grid size and seed as the only knobs. Read the result through each cell's wall flags.
useCases: Maze levels or dungeon corridors with a guaranteed solution.
A layout where you need to know a route always exists.
A base to add loops or rooms to, once the perfect maze is not what you want.

gotchas.title: Perfect means no loops, which reads as tedious at scale
gotchas.body: Exactly one route between any two points is mathematically tidy and unfun to walk in a large maze. Knocking out a few extra walls afterwards is the usual fix.

gotchas.title: Recursive backtracking favours long corridors
gotchas.body: It is a property of the algorithm, not a setting. A different algorithm is the answer if you want a different character.
